end.name: Al-Amirya (Amreya) LPG/Butane Extraction Plant, Merghem area, Amreya, Alexandria Governorate
end.coord_basis: Same Amreya town-center coordinate (Wikipedia) -- the plant is described only as sited in the Merghem area of Amreya, west of Alexandria; no independent facility-level coordinate found that would separate it from WDGC.

sheet_conflicts: StartLocation='Rashid' is substantively wrong, not just a misspelling. Egypt Oil & Gas's 'green light' article confirms this 5km link is a distinct, later spur built specifically to feed the Al-Amirya butane plant, separate from the 70km/30in Rashid-to-WDGC line (that's the sibling row, P6703). Quote: GASCO's original line 'to transfer the gases of the Raven field in the Rashid area to the Western Desert gas complex' has 'a length of 70 km' -- that describes P6703, not this row. This row is described as GASCO's 'phase two': feeding 'the Al-Amirya gas plant with quantities of up to 100 million cubic feet per day from the Raven field.' Rashid town is 40+ km from the Amreya industrial zone -- far too far for a 5km pipe. GEM's StartLocation='Rashid' most likely copy-inherited the field-of-origin label from sibling P6703 rather than describing this segment's physical start point. (Note for whoever handles attribute fields, out of this task's endpoints-only scope: the sourced diameter here is 30in, not the prior suggestion's 18in.)
notes: Confirms and firms up a prior ROUTE_PARTIAL suggestion with two additional independent Egypt Oil & Gas articles plus Wikipedia for the town coordinate. WDGC and the Amreya LPG/butane plant are both GASCO facilities co-located in the same Merghem/Amreya industrial zone southwest of Alexandria (the 'GASCO Plants in Western Desert, Amreya Produce 26.6 M tons' piece treats them as a paired complex under one production tally). No independently-sourced facility-level coordinates distinguish the two sites, so both endpoints share the same Amreya town-center coordinate -- a true two-point great-circle line from these coordinates would collapse to ~0km, which accurately reflects that this is a short intra-industrial-zone connector, not a research gap. RouteAccuracy should stay 'low'; a human/GIS pass over satellite imagery of the Merghem/Amreya complex would be needed to actually separate the two sites spatially for a meaningful route line.

sheet_conflicts: No public source names a single 'Edku-Gamasa' or 'Idku-Gamasa' pipeline as such. Egypt's own published gas-project lists (GASCO's official pipelines page, and petro-news.com's national gas-grid project rundown) instead show these two towns each anchoring a DIFFERENT, shorter, differently-paired line: 'Edco/Abu-Hommus' (~29-30km -- matches sibling GEM row P7567, Idku-Abu Hummus) and 'Gamasa-Feinosa' (34km, supplying West Damietta power station -- not connected to Idku at all). Neither list contains a ~121km line joining Idku and Gamasa directly. The great-circle distance between the two town centers (~117km) is close to the sheet's 121km, which is consistent with GEM's row describing a long coastal corridor spanning several actual named segments/pipelines end-to-end rather than one single constructed pipe -- flagging for human review as a possible network/segment-granularity question, not a sourcing failure.
notes: GASCO's own pipelines list page (gasco.com.eg) has a broken cert chain / times out on direct fetch, so it is not usable as a citable [ref] here; the Edco/Abu-Hommus and Gamasa-Feinosa corroboration instead comes from petro-news.com's national gas-project rundown. Endpoints are town-center coordinates only (no facility-level siting found); treat any drawn geometry as low RouteAccuracy, endpoints rung only, and flag the sheet_conflicts note above for whoever reviews this row's classification.

notes: Strong direct hit: Egypt Oil & Gas's feature 'Egypt's Gas Distribution Network, An Intricate Economic Web' explicitly names 'Damanhur-Tanta' as one of Egypt's 10 main Nile Delta gas transmission lines (capacity 700.1 mmcf/d, the largest of the group listed), confirming this is a real, named, standalone trunk line, not merely a sheet hypothesis (sheet StartLocation/EndLocation were blank; PipelineName already said Damanhur-Tanta). Great-circle distance between the two town centers is ~58km, closely matching the sheet's 60km length -- a very good fit for a direct point-to-point line. On the hint (GulfPub 'Idku-Tanta Pipeline', 108km): the same Egypt Oil & Gas article lists 'Alexandria Network-Damanhur' and 'Damanhur-Tanta' as TWO SEPARATE named segments, more consistent with P8019 being its own discrete Damanhur-Tanta trunk within the broader delta grid (with gas reaching Tanta via Damanhur from multiple upstream directions, Idku included) than a literal 'Damanhur-Tanta portion' carved out of one distinct 108km GulfPub-only 'Idku-Tanta' line. No independent public source was found naming a 108km 'Idku-Tanta' line by that exact name, so the GulfPub product itself is neither confirmed nor refuted here -- but the Damanhur-Tanta segment is independently well-attested regardless. Facility-level (compressor/valve site) coordinates were not found in public sources; both endpoints are town-center approximations, standard for a rung-4 (endpoints/great-circle) candidate.

end.name: Mahmoudia (El Mahmoudiyah) Power Station, Beheira Governorate
end.coord_basis: Wikipedia 'El Mahmoudiyah' infobox town-center coordinate (verified live fetch: 31.18389N 30.52417E), used as an approximation for the power station named after and sited at this town. No independent facility-gate coordinate was found.

notes: Located and fetched the actual public source the prior_suggestion could not find: the World Bank's Environmental & Social Impact Assessment for the Egyptian Natural Gas Company's EG-Giza North Power Project (P116194), disclosed 2017-07-10. It confirms, in GASCO's own words, the exact 3-segment corridor the prior work inferred: (1) 42in pipeline, 27km, 'starts...in Rashid Petroleum Company facility area, east to Edko City...to the south crossing the international coastal road, Alexandria/Rashid Railway, and Bousily Drain...till it reaches National Natural Gas Network Facility area, to the north of Bisintaway Village'; (2) 30in pipeline, 17km, from a valve room near Izbat Abdel Razeq/Hommosy 'parallel to Kom Al Gharaq Canal until it reaches Dairut Power Station'; (3) 16in pipeline, 7km, from a valve room on that line, crossing Mahmoudia Canal, 'until it reaches the pressure reduction station inside the power station' (Mahmoudia power station). Segment total 27+17+7=51km vs the sheet's 52km -- a very close match, supporting that GEM's single P7580 row represents this ENTIRE chain end-to-end (Rashid Petroleum Company facility -> Mahmoudia Power Station), not just the final 7km leg. On 'Dairut Power Station': confirmed via separate research that Dairut/Dayrut is a real, well-known town in ASSIUT Governorate (27.567N 30.817E) roughly 400km south of this Beheira corridor -- clearly not the same place. A large (2,250MW) 'Dairut IPP' CCGT power project (Acwa Power) also exists, reported near Assiut/Luxor -- also unrelated; it postdates this 2016-17 ESIA and is a much larger, separate, later project. Every other named feature in this ESIA's routing (Bousily Drain, Edko Drain, Kom Al Gharaq Canal, Bisintaway, Izbat Abdel Razeq) is a local Beheira Nile Delta feature, so 'Dairut Power Station' here is almost certainly a distinct, small, local Beheira facility that happens to share the Dairut/Dayrut name, or a rough machine-translation artifact in the ESIA's English rendering -- not the Assiut town or the Acwa IPP. Since it functions only as an interior tie-in on the same chain continuing to Mahmoudia PS (not a separate spur), it does not change the two-point start/end determination for a great-circle candidate. Recommend a human note flag on 'Dairut Power Station' for anyone later attempting a traced (not great-circle) route, since its exact siting is still not pinned to a coordinate.
